action.description: Challenging high octane gameplay, such as fighting, shooting, racing, exploding

adventure.description: Exploration, main character, rpg elements. Adventure games are about the emotion of being in an expansive environment and being a hero. Less intense gameplay than action

arcade.description: Classic challenging gameplay, such as shoot-em-up, themepark and festival classics, often single-mechanic gameplay that repeats in high frequency.

cooking.description: Cooking games are about cooking, serving, and managing a restaurant or kitchen

farm.description: Focused on farming or farming-adjacent. Plant, collect, sell. Manage resources. Includes games that are farming gameplay reskined as other themes

horror.description: Scary, dark, violent, creepy, haunted. Can sometimes be funny, but usually contains jump scares. Horror games are about the theme, can have a variety of gameplay mechanics

meme.description: Gimicky or uses popular meme elements. Quirky games that don't fit anywhere else

platformer.description: The core mechanic is running and jumping onto platforms with a main character

puzzle.description: Mentally challenging. Often spatial challenges, sometimes with math, other times sorting, sequencing or merging challenges, question-based, etc.

rhythm.description: Games requiring timing to the beat

simulation.description: Gameplay simulates a real-world concept, such as tycoon, god-sim, city building. Sometimes resource management and operationalization, other times can be sandbox

sports.description: Related to classical sports, such as soccer, basketball, but also gymnastics, pool, etc.

survival.description: Centered around a main character or troop of characters. Limited resources, crafting, death and defeat, rpg elements

tactics.description: Strategy and tactical gameplay. Auto-battler, card battler, tower defense, turn-based combat, etc

zen.description: Relaxing gameplay, without competition, combat or time preassure. Often sandbox, decoration or exploration

incremental.description: Clicker and similar gameplay. The core theme is 'number goes up'. Spend resource to buy upgrades, click to get resource, or get resource passively

creative.description: Self-expressive artistic experience. Drawing, painting, pixel-art, collage, scrapbook, etc. Can have specific challenges, but sometimes not

chess.description: Specifically games that center around Chess

educational.description: Math, word and trivia games that center around question and answer. Sometimes with multiple choice and other times with a field to type answers.

merge.description: Games where the central mechanic is merging: Combine smaller objects to make bigger ones (or low tier combine to make high tier).

chat.description: Games in which you primarily chat or role-play with one or more characters.

toys.description: A simple interactive experience with no purpose other than pure fun: no winning or losing, no fail state, no levels, no currency or upgrade shops, no leaderboards. Just a single, mindlessly entertaining mechanic that is inherently enjoyable without any overall goal. Physics play (spinning, dragging and dropping, pushing and pulling, popping, smashing, ragdolls, destruction) and creative play (doodling, drawing, coloring, tracing, decorating) both count. A passive tally of actions is fine, but if the game presents a score to beat, a leaderboard, levels to clear, or any way to fail or win, it is NOT toys.

minecraft.description: A Minecraft game or a direct clone of one. Strong signals: 'Minecraft', 'craft' or 'mine' in the title; a first-person or third-person 3D voxel world made of cube blocks that the player breaks and places; open-world exploration with mining, crafting, building, and surviving mobs. Do NOT tag a game just because is blocky, low-poly, has cubes, or mentions Minecraft in passing — a voxel racer, a block puzzle, or a 2D platformer with pixel blocks is not minecraft.

themes.definition: Mood, aesthetic, and gameplay themes that describe the game's feel and content. Multiple themes can apply.

valid_values.action: Challenging high-octane gameplay — fighting, shooting, racing, explosions
valid_values.adventure: Exploration, main character, rpg elements. Adventure games are about the emotion of being in an expansive environment and being a hero. Less intense gameplay than action
valid_values.arcade: Classic challenging gameplay, such as shoot-em-up, themepark and festival classics, often single-mechanic gameplay that repeats in high frequency.
valid_values.cooking: Cooking games are about cooking, serving, and managing a restaurant or kitchen
valid_values.farm: Focused on farming or farming-adjacent. Plant, collect, sell. Manage resources. Includes games that are farming gameplay reskinned as other themes
valid_values.horror: Scary, dark, violent, creepy, haunted. Can sometimes be funny, but usually contains jump scares. Horror games are about the theme, can have a variety of gameplay mechanics
valid_values.meme: Gimmicky or uses popular meme elements. Quirky games that don't fit anywhere else
valid_values.platformer: The core mechanic is running and jumping onto platforms with a main character
valid_values.puzzle: Mentally challenging. Often spatial challenges, sometimes with math, other times sorting, sequencing or merging challenges, question-based, etc.
valid_values.rhythm: Games requiring timing to the beat
valid_values.simulation: Gameplay simulates a real-world concept, such as tycoon, god-sim, city building. Resource management and systems-thinking, sometimes sandbox
valid_values.sports: Related to classical sports, such as soccer, basketball, but also gymnastics, pool, etc.
valid_values.survival: Centered around a main character or troop of characters. Limited resources, crafting, death and defeat, rpg elements
valid_values.tactics: Strategy and tactical gameplay. Auto-battler, card battler, tower defense, turn-based combat, etc.
valid_values.zen: Relaxing gameplay, without competition, combat or time pressure. Often sandbox, decoration or exploration
valid_values.incremental: Clicker and similar gameplay. The core theme is 'number goes up'. Spend resource to buy upgrades, click to get resource, or get resource passively
valid_values.creative: Self-expressive artistic experience. Drawing, painting, pixel-art, collage, scrapbook, etc. Can have specific challenges, but sometimes not
valid_values.chess: Chess or chess-derived strategy — pieces, boards, and positional tactics
valid_values.educational: Math, word and trivia games that center around question and answer. Sometimes with multiple choice and other times with a field to type answers.
valid_values.merge: Games where the central mechanic is merging: Combine smaller objects to make bigger ones (or low tier combine to make high tier).

genre.definition: The primary genre classification of the game. Choose the most specific genre that best describes the core gameplay experience.

valid_values.Action RPG: Real-time combat with RPG character progression
valid_values.Adventure: Exploration and narrative-driven gameplay with a main character
valid_values.Arcade: Classic score-chasing reflex gameplay, often single-mechanic
valid_values.Auto Battler: Units fight automatically; player manages composition and strategy
valid_values.Base Building: Construct and expand a base or settlement
valid_values.Beat 'em up: Melee combat against waves of enemies, side-scrolling
valid_values.Board Game: Digital adaptation of a tabletop board game
valid_values.Breakout: Bounce a ball to destroy blocks (Breakout/Arkanoid style)
valid_values.Card Game: Card-based gameplay — hand management, deck play
valid_values.City Builder: Plan and grow a city or civilization
valid_values.Clicker: Tap or click repeatedly; number goes up
valid_values.Cooking: Cook, serve, and manage a kitchen or restaurant
valid_values.Deckbuilder: Construct a card deck through play and use it in combat
valid_values.Dungeon Crawler: Explore procedural dungeons, fight monsters, collect loot
valid_values.Educational: Math, word, trivia, or quiz-based learning
valid_values.Endless Runner: Run indefinitely, dodge obstacles, score goes up
valid_values.Escape Room: Solve interconnected puzzles to escape a space
valid_values.Farming Sim: Plant, tend, harvest, and sell crops
valid_values.Fighting: 1v1 or team combat with dedicated move sets
valid_values.Hack and Slash: Fast melee combat against many enemies simultaneously
valid_values.Hidden Object: Find specific items within a detailed scene
valid_values.Incremental: Passive or active resource accumulation with upgrades
valid_values.Match 3: Swap and match three or more identical tiles
valid_values.Merge: Combine identical objects to create higher-tier ones
valid_values.Metroidvania: Exploration with ability gating and backtracking
valid_values.Pinball: Keep a ball in play with flippers, hit targets for score
valid_values.Platformer: Run and jump across platforms with a main character
valid_values.Point & Click: Navigate scenes and solve puzzles by clicking objects
valid_values.Puzzle: Logic and spatial problem-solving as the core loop
valid_values.Racing: Compete for speed against opponents or the clock
valid_values.Rhythm: Hit inputs in time to music beats
valid_values.RPG: Character stats, leveling, and narrative progression
valid_values.Run 'n' Gun: Run and shoot simultaneously in action levels
valid_values.Sandbox: Open freeform play with no fixed objectives
valid_values.Shoot 'em up: Shoot waves of enemies from a scrolling perspective
valid_values.Shooter: Aim and shoot from a fixed or free-roaming perspective (not a shmup)
valid_values.Simulation: Simulate a real-world system — tycoon, god-game, city-building
valid_values.Sokoban: Push boxes onto targets in confined grid spaces
valid_values.Sports: Soccer, basketball, or other classical sports
valid_values.Stealth: Avoid detection; sneaking is the core mechanic
valid_values.Strategy: Plan and outmaneuver — resource management, map control
valid_values.Survival: Gather resources, craft, and survive against threats
valid_values.Survival Horror: Survive in a terrifying environment with limited resources
valid_values.Tower Defense: Place units or towers to stop waves of enemies
valid_values.Twin Stick Shooter: Move with one joystick, aim/shoot with the other
valid_values.Tycoon: Build and manage a business for profit
valid_values.Typing Game: Type words or letters as the core mechanic
valid_values.Visual Novel: Story-driven with dialogue choices and branching paths
valid_values.Zen: Relaxing, low-pressure, often no lose state

art_style.definition: The visual aesthetic style of the game.

valid_values.cartoon: Bold outlines, bright flat colors, exaggerated proportions
valid_values.minimalist: Simple geometric shapes, clean sparse design
valid_values.neon: Glowing neon colors on dark backgrounds
valid_values.pixel-art: Retro pixelated aesthetic with visible pixel grid
valid_values.none: No distinct or consistent art style

setting.definition: The world or aesthetic identity the game takes place in. Use 'none' if no clear setting applies.

valid_values.anime: Japanese animation setting and culture — manga visuals, anime tropes, Japanese world-building
valid_values.historical: Past eras — ancient, classical, or early modern periods
valid_values.none: No distinct world setting or aesthetic

tone.definition: The emotional register of the game — how it feels to play.

difficulty.definition: The skill and attention demand placed on the player.

valid_values.casual: Anyone can play, low skill demand, very forgiving
valid_values.moderate: Some challenge, requires attention and practice
valid_values.challenging: Demands real skill, regular failures expected
valid_values.hardcore: High skill ceiling, punishing mistakes, mastery required

main_activity.definition: What the player does moment-to-moment as the core gameplay loop.

valid_values.exploration: Move through and discover an environment

progression.definition: How the game rewards or advances the player over time. Use 'none' if there is no meaningful progression system. This vocabulary applies to both primary and secondary progression.

loop_length.definition: The typical duration of a single play session or meaningful game loop.

valid_values.open-ended: No defined end, player decides when to stop

learning_curve.definition: How long it takes for a new player to understand and meaningfully engage with the core mechanic.

valid_values.instant: Self-evident in seconds, no instruction needed
valid_values.moderate: Takes several sessions to fully grasp

primary_control.definition: The main way the player interacts with the game on mobile.

valid_values.drag: Pick up and place items by dragging
valid_values.dual joystick: Two virtual joysticks for movement and aim

secondary_control.definition: A meaningful secondary control scheme if the game uses two distinct input methods. Use 'none' if there is only one control scheme.

valid_values.drag: Pick up and place items by dragging

perspective.definition: The visual perspective from which the game is presented.

valid_values.ui_based: No world perspective — purely UI/menu-driven (e.g. card games, clickers)

polish_level.definition: How much attention to detail the game has beyond its basic implementation. Most games are 'standard'. Only assign 'high' or 'exceptional' when there are clear extra touches — tutorials, particle effects, satisfying audio feedback, smooth animations, or other signs of deliberate craft.

valid_values.low: Minimal effort beyond making the game functional. May have basic sound or visuals, but little craft or attention to feel. Often true.
valid_values.standard: The default. The game is complete and plays well with VFX, SFX, and all other standard aspects of polished games, but does not go above and beyond. Applies to the majority of games.
valid_values.high: Noticeable extra craft - well thought out 'juicy' feedback for interactions, optimized loading times, leaderboard support, etc. Somewhat rare.
valid_values.exceptional: A high level of polish akin to a professionally released mobile game — multiple layered polish systems working together. The code is clearly very thoght out to make sure each aspect of gameplay shines. Very rare.
